requirement: Add retry support for firmware download when the transfer fails.

evidence.excerpt:
nvme-fw-download(1)
===================

NAME
----
nvme-fw-download - Download all or a portion of an nvme firmware image.

SYNOPSIS
--------
[verse]
'nvme' [<global-options>] 'fw download' <device>
			[--fw=<firmware-file> | -f <firmware-file>]
			[--xfer=<transfer-size> | -x <transfer-size>]
			[--offset=<offset> | -O <offset>]
			[--stream]

DESCRIPTION
-----------
The Firmware Image Download command is used to download all or a portion
of the firmware image for a future update to the controller. The Firmware
Image Download command may be submitted while other commands on the Admin
Submission Queue or I/O Submission Queues are outstanding. The Firmware
Image Download command copies the new firmware image (in whole or in part)
to the controller.

def test_download_failure_stops_the_transfer(self):
        """A rejected transfer is reported and the commit is not attempted."""
        path = self.firmware(size=3 * _FW_CHUNK, name="fwfail.bin")
        self.server.fw_download_status = SC_INVALID_FIELD
        result = self.run_plugin_cmd(_DOWNLOAD, args=f"-f {path} -s ALL")

        self.assertNotEqual(result.returncode, 0)
        self.assertEqual(len(self.downloads()), 1,
                         "the transfer continued past a rejected chunk")
        self.assertEqual(self.commits(), [],
                         "the image was committed despite a failed transfer")

To increase the likelihood of success, you may want to pre-allocate a
number of huge pages before initiating the firmware download:

  echo 20 > /proc/sys/vm/nr_hugepages

For more details, refer to:
https://www.kernel.org/doc/Documentation/vm/hugetlbpage.txt

The bare 'nvme fw-download' form (without a space) still works as a deprecated
alias and will be removed in a future major version. New scripts should
use 'nvme fw download' instead.

OPTIONS
-------
-f <firmware-file>::
--fw=<firmware-file>::
	Required argument. This specifies the path to the device's
	firmware file on your system that will be read by the program
	and sent to the device.

-x <transfer-size>::
--xfer=<transfer-size>::
	This specifies the size to split each transfer. This is useful if
	the device has a max transfer size requirement for firmware. It

defaults to 4k.

-O <offset>::
--offset=<offset>::
	This specifies the starting offset in dwords. This is really only
	useful if your firmware is split in multiple files; otherwise
	the offset starts at zero and automatically adjusts based on the
	'xfer' size given.

--stream::
	Read and download one transfer-sized portion of the firmware image at
	a time instead of mapping the complete image into memory. This avoids
	the huge page requirement and limits memory use to the transfer size.

include::global-options.txt[]

EXAMPLES
--------
* Transfer a firmware size 128KiB at a time:
+
------------
# nvme fw download /dev/nvme0 --fw=/path/to/nvme.fw --xfer=0x20000
------------

questions.question: The core command already makes up to three attempts per chunk. Is the requested change a configurable attempt/backoff policy, or support for a specific failing command/path that this loop does not recover?
questions.reason: Source establishes that retry support exists but the request does not identify what existing behavior is inadequate.

alternatives.answer: Make existing retry count or timing configurable
alternatives.effect: Modify the current helper and CLI configuration while retaining its status handling and chunk boundaries.

alternatives.answer: Recover a specific failure or another vendor/transport path
alternatives.effect: First identify the affected path and error outcome; inspect that implementation and its applicable specification before changing retry eligibility.

interpretations.text: The canonical firmware-download command already retries through fw_download_single. The requirement needs refinement into a change to existing retry behavior rather than the addition of a second retry loop.

warnings: Semantic interpretation and question selection require a configured model.
Static symbol/call observations do not prove runtime reachability or behavior.
Evidence is a snapshot; refresh before acting if the workspace changes.
Model review and matching quotations do not prove semantic correctness.

constraints.text: Existing retry policy permits at most three total submission attempts per chunk; three attempts should not be described as three extra retries.
constraints.applicability: plugins/fw/fw-plugin.c::fw_download_single at this revision; max_retries is 3 in the same excerpt.
constraints.why_relevant: Adding another outer retry loop could multiply the number of submissions.

constraints.text: The current helper stops resending NVMe errors carrying DNR.
constraints.applicability: Positive NVMe-type error responses in fw_download_single; not a verified statement of all transport behavior.
constraints.why_relevant: A retry change must account for the existing distinction between resendable errors and DNR responses.

constraints.text: An overlapping-range response is either accepted with ignore_ovr or made non-retryable otherwise.
constraints.applicability: Non-ignored overlapping firmware-range errors in the existing core helper.
constraints.why_relevant: Blind resubmission can repeat overwrites; current code has a dedicated recovery policy.

constraints.text: The caller stops advancing chunks when fw_download_single returns an error.
constraints.applicability: The core fw_download chunk loop, including its stream and mapped-buffer paths.
constraints.why_relevant: Retrying a chunk must not be confused with advancing to the next firmware offset.

unresolved: No NVMe specification revision was supplied; DNR and overlapping-range behavior above are source observations, not independently verified normative requirements.
Vendor-specific firmware commands are not established to share the core helper; the Micron seed test is insufficient evidence for a repository-wide retry policy.
